newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium ends down on LME in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium ends down on LME in thin trade.

text.p: Tokyo aluminium futures ended lower across the board on Tuesday, as a decline in London Metal Exchange three-month metal prices on Monday triggered selling orders from local investors, traders said.
Prices were 1.0 to 2.5 yen lower, with the benchmark February 1998 contract down 1.9 yen at 205.1 yen per kg.
Trading was thin. The day's volume was 3,890 lots, up from 2,517 on Monday but sharply down from 19,645 last Monday.
The three-month aluminium contact on the LME ended at $1,549 a tonne on Monday, down $15 from the previous close.
"The yen's firmer tone partly supported the market. But local investors are losing interest in the Tokyo aluminium futures contract," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
Open interest as of April 14 was 19,575 lots. TOCOM launched the aluminium contract last Monday, but the current bearish trend in the base metals market is discouraging local investors, traders said.
